Subject: C-suite approval needed: Oversized discount request — Hosted API renewal

Hi Sara / SustainTech team —

Thanks for the productive conversation last week. As discussed, SustainTech is targeting a multi-year renewal for Hosted API with a material uptick in usage (estimated 2.5B tokens/month year 1). To secure the commitment they have asked for a 30% list-rate concession across the multi-year term.

Summary of the ask:
- Product: Hosted API (text generation + streaming)
- Term: 36 months, annual auto-renew
- Commitment: Minimum spend guarantee equivalent to 2.5B tokens/month first year, escalating by 15%/yr
- Requested concession: 30% off published usage rates (upfront billing preferred)

Why this needs exec signoff: Redwood policy requires >20% pricing concession to be approved by the C-suite / Deal Desk execs (impact to ARR forecasts and margins). Rishi and I ran a quick unit-econ check — at 30% the effective blended CPM falls below our target but the account is strategic in health-tech vertical and could be an anchor in the enterprise segment.

Attachments: sustaintech-pricing-deck.pdf (proposed redlines), SustainTech_COMMITMENT_LOI.docx (signed LOI draft).

Request: Can you review and confirm whether we can approve up to 30% or if we should counter at a lower concession (recommended 25–27%) with additional commercial protections (shorter payback, milestone-based credits, performance SLA floors)? Need a decision by EOD Wed 10/03 to keep momentum.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Laura —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming SustainTech is ready to move quickly and prefers a single-vendor model for inference. A few clarifications from our side before you escalate:
- The 36-month term is flexible if we get price certainty and a data residency addendum.
- The 30% ask is a firm target from our CFO; they view the long-term commitment and projected token growth as justification.
- We prefer upfront annual payment but can consider quarterly invoicing tied to committed spend.

We're happy to sign an LOI this week if Redwood can commit to a discount in the 27–30% range and include standard SOC2 + GDPR artifacts in the contract. Would you be able to share the preferred concession and any non-standard clauses you would require?

Quick internal read: I ran the numbers with finance. Key points:
- At 30% off list, 36-month term, projected NRR and unit economics are below our threshold (negative contribution first 12 months on conservative ramp).
- Risk mitigation options we should insist on if we go beyond 20%: upfront or annual prepayment with breakage protection, minimum committed spend floors, and a revenue share for early overages.
- Recommended concession band for approval: 25%–27% with the following conditions: 1) annual prepayment equal to year-1 committed spend, 2) a 12-month minimum commitment with termination penalties, 3) standardized SLA credits only (no bespoke uptime SLAs).

Please escalate to Markus and include the commercial terms list and the LOI. I'll attach the quick P&L we used (summaries in the attached pricing deck).

Team —

I've reviewed the summary, the P&L and SustainTech's LOI. I will approve a 27% off-list concession on the following explicit conditions:
1) Year-1 prepayment equal to 100% of the committed year-1 spend (non-refundable, applied against usage).
2) Minimum 12-month guaranteed commitment with liquidated damages equal to 50% of remaining committed value if they terminate early (standardized language).
3) No additional SLA or bespoke security commitments beyond our standard SOC2/GDPR artifacts.
4) All commercial terms to be processed through Deal Desk and Legal for standard contract addendum (no side letters).

If SustainTech agrees to these guardrails, we can finalize and return an executed LOI and then move to DocuSign for the full contract. Rishi — please prepare the redline and the final summary for legal. Laura — please confirm with SustainTech and get the LOI signed.
